title: When dust growth takes over: the origin of dust in post-reionization galaxies
summary: The post-reionization epoch ($z\sim4$-6) marks a critical phase in galaxy evolution, during which galaxies rapidly assemble their stellar mass, enrich their interstellar medium, and build up substantial dust reservoirs. The physical processes responsible for such rapid dust enrichment remain uncertain. We investigate the dust enrichment history of the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST (ACJ) sample using the semi-analytic galaxy formation model GAlaxy Evolution and Assembly (GAEA), which follows galaxy assembly, chemical enrichment, and dust evolution. We select model galaxies matching the observed stellar masses, star formation rates, and metallicities of the ACJ sample, compare their dust properties with observed scaling relations, and trace their enrichment histories and environments. The model reproduces the observed dust mass-stellar mass relation and the dust-to-stellar mass, dust-to-gas, and dust-to-metal ratios as functions of stellar mass and metallicity. Reproducing these constraints requires efficient dust growth in the interstellar medium; stellar dust production alone cannot account for the observed dust reservoirs, even under the most optimistic assumptions. The combination of stellar mass, star formation rate, and metallicity provides a good predictor of galaxy dust content. Our model suggests rapid dust build-up consistent with the previously noted rapid metal enrichment, with evidence for a transition around $z\sim8$-9 below which dust growth becomes the dominant dust formation channel. Finally, ACJ-like galaxies preferentially reside in locally overdense environments, suggesting that environment may have contributed to their accelerated evolution. Taken together, these results support rapid and coupled stellar, metal, and dust build-up in ACJ galaxies during the post-reionization era.

title: Bridging Theory and Observation: Synthetic Far-infrared Insights into Star Formation Efficiency
summary: The star formation efficiency per free-fall time ($ε_{\rm ff}$) quantifies how efficiently giant molecular clouds (GMCs) convert gas into stars and is often observed to be orders of magnitude lower than expected for free-fall collapse. Observers typically estimate $ε_{\rm ff}$ by mapping far-infrared (FIR) dust emission to infer gas surface densities ($Σ_{\rm gas}$) and counting embedded protostars, assuming simplified lifetimes and masses. Using the fiducial STARFORGE radiation-magnetohydrodynamics simulation of an $M_{\rm cl} = 2\times10^4 M_\odot$ GMC that self-consistently models star cluster formation and stellar feedback, we generate synthetic FIR observations and apply the same methodologies used in GMC surveys to investigate this discrepancy. We present the first $ε_{\rm ff}-Σ_{\rm gas}$ analysis in a fully feedback-regulated GMC simulation that resolves the formation of stellar systems. Our synthetic measurements reproduce the low observationally inferred efficiencies, showing that feedback-regulated star formation naturally produces $ε_{\rm ff} \sim 1-3\%$ without requiring extreme initial conditions. We also find that $ε_{\rm ff}$ varies strongly over a GMC's lifetime, suggesting that much of the observed scatter reflects evolutionary sampling rather than intrinsic cloud-to-cloud differences. Finally, by comparing observational and simulation definitions, we show that methodological assumptions introduce systematic biases, with a transition near $\log Σ_{\rm gas} \approx 2.3 M_\odot {\rm pc}^{-2}$ that depends on resolution. Above this threshold, the smoothing of dense structure increases both the inferred free-fall time and enclosed gas, with the latter dominating and suppressing $ε_{\rm ff}$. Below the threshold, the discrepancies are primarily driven by star formation rate assumptions.

title: A Burst of Reionization in the Dark Ages
summary: Primordial overdensities at small scales can be significantly larger than those observed at large scales. As a result, they can collapse much earlier, at redshifts $z \sim 100$. In these collapsed halos, stars and black holes can form, where they can then contribute to an early reionization of the universe. If this epoch is temporary, the free electrons will recombine yielding a low level of ionization leading into cosmic dawn. This contributes to the optical depth of the universe, and adds more weakly to low-$\ell$ polarization signals of ionization compared to later sources. We study the effects of a redshift-localized source of reionization $Δτ_{burst}$ in the context of a broad suite of cosmological data to constrain this scenario, finding a preference of approximately $\sim 2-2.5σ$ for a new contribution. Regardless of Planck reprocessing used (PR3 - SRoll2+plik or PR4 - LoLLiPoP+CamSpec/HiLLiPoP), the results are consistent, favoring a new contribution $Δτ_{burst} \sim 0.012$ ($0.001 < Δτ_{burst} < 0.022$ at 95\%) and a similar total optical depth $τ\sim 0.073$. The precise era of reionization is somewhat discrepant depending on the higher-$\ell$ reprocessing used, with HiLLiPoP favoring $z\sim 45$, CamSpec $z\sim 100$ and plik $z\sim 165$. If such a source is present at $40\lesssim z\lesssim150$, LiteBIRD should be able to detect it, while Simons Observatory should also constrain it.

title: FlyHack: Stress-Testing Mechanistic Claims in a Connectome-Constrained Visual Model
summary: Connectome-constrained neural networks make biological components directly accessible to intervention, but their mechanistic conclusions can still depend on the comparison model, intervention, circuit representation and trained solution. We stress-test these dependencies in flyvis, a \emph{Drosophila} motion-vision model, using its 50-model ensemble, task-matched causal CNN controls and replicated interventions. At the level of model behaviour, three-level reverse-phi reversal in flyvis is strongly period- and velocity-dependent and also appears in task-matched CNNs; neither family reproduces the fly's stationary-sawtooth response. Adversarial direction reversal requires a perturbation bound of 0.21--0.27 times stimulus contrast in flyvis versus 0.13--0.25 in CNNs, but the gap over a parameter-matched CNN largely closes for larger CNNs. At the level of mechanism, matching attribution to the intervention matters: for held-out-mean replacement, first-order edge attribution patching reaches pooled AUROC 0.970 and Spearman 0.872, versus 0.933 and 0.126 when its zero-aligned score is evaluated against the same ground truth. Circuit conclusions also vary with representation and ensemble member. Greedy cell-type sets meet a model-relative T4/T5 tuning criterion in 25 of 50 models, while T4/T5 output silencing reduces the tested optic-flow behaviour to at most two of eight clips in 40. In six models where the cell-type search first succeeds, the corresponding connection sets can be pruned to 13--31 added classes; under an additional two-sided response-amplitude check, only two of those six first-success cell-type sets still meet the tuning threshold. These results support a narrower use of connectome-constrained models: they make mechanistic hypotheses directly testable, but the resulting claims must be scoped to the model family, intervention, representation and trained solution.

title: On the Performance of Randomly Generated Codebooks in Near-Field Communications
summary: Near-field communication with large antenna arrays requires beamforming techniques that account for spherical wavefront effects. While predefined codebooks are widely used in multiple-antenna wireless systems, the performance of randomly generated codebooks in the near-field region has not been investigated. In this work, we study four randomly generated codebooks for near-field communications: random vector quantization (RVQ), random phase (RP), random far-field (RFF), and random near-field (RNF) codebooks. We use the known RVQ gain distribution as a benchmark. For RP, we derive a large-array bulk approximation and characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RNF, we characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RFF, we derive an analytical approximation for the maximum achievable beamforming gain when far-field beams are used to serve near-field users, along with the corresponding maximizing far-field direction. We also analyze the maximum-gain scaling with codebook size. Monte Carlo simulations verify the analytical results and show that RVQ and RP degrade significantly as the array size increases, while RNF achieves the most favorable high-gain scaling. RFF can outperform RVQ and RP for finite codebook sizes, but its maximum gain saturates below one due to the phase mismatch between the far-field beams and the near-field channel. These results show how codebook structure, array size, and codebook size affect random beamforming performance in the near-field.

title: r/ADHD: Community-Based Understandings of Time Management Challenges in Digital Environments
summary: Community accounts of ADHD can complement clinical understandings by foregrounding members' own definitions of time-management difficulties and support. We used human-led, LLM-assisted thematic analysis to examine 5,379 relevant r/ADHD posts from 2020 to 2025. Across five challenge and nine strategy themes, members described difficulties beginning intended tasks, disengaging from digital media, and sustaining support. Tools often demanded the self-regulation they were meant to support, while lost time and tool breakdown carried guilt and self-blame. Members drew on people, routines, and environments alongside digital tools, often seeking advice and recognition from peers. These accounts broaden the design problem to include the practical and emotional work of sustaining support. They motivate tools that reduce this burden and evaluations that consider recovery after distraction and emotional costs alongside task outcomes.

title: Predicted state-to-state collisional rate coefficients from neural networks
summary: Molecular spectra observed in the interstellar medium are commonly analyzed using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium models, which requires accurate state-to-state collisional rate coefficients. Close-coupling calculations become prohibitively expensive for transitions from highly excited rotational states, therefore available datasets are often truncated at low initial states and temperatures; and since each new system also requires an accurate ab initio potential energy surface, many detected molecules have no collisional data. We employ two machine learning strategies to predict rotational state-to-state rate coefficients of molecules included in the train set beyond the range of initial states and temperatures computed so far, and predicting those of a molecule absent from training and validation sets. Feed-forward neural networks are trained on state-to-state de-excitation rate coefficients of 24 linear molecules colliding with para-H2. Scheme 1 includes all systems in the train+validation set, with 70%, 80%, and 90% initial-state boundaries and a 90% temperature boundary. Scheme 2 is trained on 22 systems described only by transition and molecular properties, and predicts two excluded systems, CS and CF+, whose astrophysical impact is explored with non-LTE calculations. For the 90% boundary, Scheme 1 predicts 99.4% of the test transitions within a factor of 2, and no prediction deviates from the reference value by more than a factor of 4.7. This model was used to complete 18 datasets. Scheme 2 reproduces the rate coefficients of two excluded systems within a factor of 3 for more than 92% of their transitions. Both schemes provide near-instantaneous complements to close-coupling calculations: Scheme 1 extends the range of a molecule already included in the training set with high accuracy, while Scheme 2 gives a reasonable first estimate for a molecule that has not been studied.

title: The road to $H_0$, $Ω_m$, and $w$ with a global neutrino-telescope network
summary: The newly measured correlation between the neutrino and X-ray luminosities of Seyfert galaxies has yielded the first neutrino-based measurement of the Hubble constant. Building on this result, we forecast the reach of a global neutrino-telescope network by 2030, utilizing full-sky IceCube exposures combined with KM3NeT-ARCA and Baikal-GVD. We find that this 2030 configuration sharpens the neutrino-measured Hubble constant from today's $H_0 = 66^{+44}_{-37}$ to $H_0 =66^{+15}_{-13}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. Additionally, we project that the disk-corona slope of the neutrino X-ray luminosity relation ($L_ν\propto L_X^β$) will reach $β=0.72\pm0.04$, enabling a $\geq \!5σ$ exclusion of the calorimetric value $β=1$. Finally, we show that, if a high-redshift population of neutrino sources, such as JWST's "little red dots," is identified and obeys the same luminosity relation, we can obtain a new independent measurement of the matter density $Ω_m$ and the dark energy equation-of-state parameter $w$.

title: Excitability across scales: a unifying EI model
summary: Neuronal excitability is commonly modeled using different principles at the cellular and population scales, making it difficult to study how microscopic mechanisms shape macroscopic activity. We introduce a spatiotemporal excitatory-inhibitory (EI) model that unifies these scales through a common mixed-feedback architecture. The model retains the conductance-based circuit structure of Hodgkin-Huxley models and describes intrinsic and synaptic currents through memductances whose temporal and spatial voltage dependence encodes dynamics at the relevant scale. In its minimal form, temporal excitability arises from fast excitatory feedback opposed by slower inhibitory feedback, while spatial excitability arises from short-range excitation opposed by longer-range inhibition, recovering the core lateral-inhibition motif of Amari neural fields. We show that combining these mechanisms gives rise to population excitability in strongly heterogeneous populations. In particular, the model generates population spikes that are localized in both space and time and possess population-level scales distinct from those of individual neuronal spikes, despite substantial cell-to-cell parameter variability. We then show that both intrinsic temporal excitability and spatial synaptic feedback are required for coherent mean-field events and robust spatiotemporal population rhythms. Finally, selective modulation of memductances in a subset of the population tunes the frequency of the population rhythm, illustrating how changes at the cellular scale can shape macroscopic dynamics. By separating circuit architecture from modeling scale, the proposed framework provides a physically interpretable approach to analyzing and designing neuronal excitability across scales.

title: Simultaneous Direct and Indirect Channel Estimation for RIS-Assisted MIMO Communications
summary: This paper introduces an enhanced channel estimation method for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Considering the presence of both the direct link from the base station (BS) to the user equipment (UE) and the indirect link \textit{via} the RIS, we formulate a tensor-based receiver for joint direct and indirect channel estimation called the TenDICE algorithm. The proposed receiver relies on an extended parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) tensor model for the received pilot signals, from which the involved (direct and indirect link) channels are estimated using a simple alternating least squares scheme. The proposed TenDICE method is compared with the state-of-the-art least squares (LS) method, Khatri-Rao factorization (KRF) method, enhanced trilinear alternating least squares (E-TALS), and the theoretical Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) based on normalized mean square error (NMSE) and spectral efficiency (SE). The proposed TenDICE outperforms the LS and E-TALS methods and performs similarly to the KRF methods while estimating the direct channel.

title: Incremental Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Human-in-the-Loop Decision Support
summary: We introduce iRAG, a human-in-the-loop decision-support system combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Hybrid Decision-Making. Unlike conventional RAG systems, relying on static Knowledge Bases (KBs), our proposal addresses settings where the KB is initially empty and is progressively populated through human decisions. The system stores previous decisions as retrievable precedents and moves from silent observation to evidence-grounded contestation and, finally, to autonomous handling with abstention. Against an independent baseline, iRAG matches final-decision error under 10% drift without retrieval decay and reduces it under 40% drift across all configurations. Retrieval decay improves performance on changed knowledge while increasing error on stable knowledge, evidencing a stability--plasticity trade-off rather than a general advantage. Human oversight is an architectural provision of the workflow; its usability with real human users remains to be evaluated.

title: Decomposing the Kinematics of SNR G180.0-01.7 with Medium-Resolution Spectra
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: The exceptionally large angular diameter and intrinsic optical faintness of the Galactic supernova remnant (SNR) G180.0-01.7 (S147) have historically hindered a comprehensive spectroscopic census of its filamentary structure. We present the first dedicated medium-resolution (R ~ 7500) spectroscopic study of S147 using the LAMOST Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic survey of Galactic Nebulae (MRS-N). By implementing multi-Gaussian decomposition on the H$α$, [NII], and [SII] emission complexes and applying combined spectroscopic and spatial criteria, we disentangle the shock-ionized filaments of the SNR from the pervasive foreground and background Diffuse Ionized Gas (DIG). Our analysis reveals a distinct bimodal radial velocity distribution for the SNR: a low-velocity population tracing the decelerated forward shock at a dense cavity wall, and a high-velocity population (with absolute radial velocities of ~ 70 $\pm$ 30 km/s) corresponding to ejecta within a low-density cavity. The co-existence of these populations provides kinematic evidence for the "supernova-in-a-cavity" scenario. Furthermore, we detect enhanced [SII]/H$α$ ratios in the DIG along the eastern and northern boundaries of the remnant, signaling shock compression of the ambient interstellar medium and highlighting remnant's multifaceted feedback.

title: Nailing down the Hubble constant value through time delay cosmography: A 3% measurement from SN Refsdal
comment: 8 pages, 4 figues, 1 table; submitted to A&A
summary: We present the first inference of the Hubble constant and matter density parameter from a strongly lensed supernova (SN) by exploiting the mass model of a galaxy cluster enhanced by an extended surface brightness reconstruction. This has resulted in the most precise H0 measurement from a single strong lens so far, outperforming the 3.9% result from the lensed quasar DES J048-5354. Building upon the mass model of MACS J1149.5+2223 relying on image positions only, we incorporate the surface brightness distribution of the SN Refsdal host, to infer some cosmological parameter values within a flat LCDM framework. We consider two cosmological parameterizations, with either H0 and $Ω_m$ or H0 alone treated as free parameters. We explore four different mass-model realizations to assess some of the systematic uncertainties associated with the constraint weighting and source reconstruction. Although known as one of the main systematic effects, we deliberately keep the cluster total mass parametrization fixed to that of the previously published point-like mass model to enable a fair comparison. This reveals that incorporating 77,000 HST pixels reduces the uncertainty on the inferred value of H0 by a factor of 2.0. Our final measurements are $H_0=65.0^{+2.0}_{-1.8}$ km/s/Mpc and $Ω_m=0.30^{+0.08}_{-0.09}$, in agreement with previous results from lensed SNe. This corresponds to a substantially improved precision, reaching a remarkable 3.0% uncertainty on the value of H0. The contributions of the uncertainties on the lens total mass and on the measured time delays to the final H0 error are now comparable, indicating that future improvements will depend on more precise time-delay measurements and continued control of systematic effects. With sub-percent time-delay values reachable at cluster-scale, this mass model approach has the power to lead to unprecedentedly precise H0 measurements.

title: Beyond Anxiety and Avoidance: A Dynamic Feedback-Regulation Framework for Adult Romantic Attachment
comment: Submitted to New Ideas in Psychology
summary: Adult attachment is commonly represented by attachment anxiety and avoidance, but these person-level dimensions do not by themselves specify how momentary relational conditions are perceived, compared with desired conditions, translated into action, and updated after interpersonal feedback. We present the Attachment Regulation and Control (ARC) framework as an integrative feedback-regulation account that makes these temporal assumptions explicit and empirically testable. In ARC, control refers to feedback-based regulation toward relational goals in the control-theoretic sense, not interpersonal dominance, coercion, or a generalized need for control. ARC does not claim a novel control-system architecture. Instead, it synthesizes established control-theoretic attachment ideas, secure-base representations, perceived partner responsiveness, relational discrepancy, dyadic regulation, and recovery into a parsimonious sequence for adult romantic relationships: perceived relational state, desired relational state, discrepancy, regulatory action, partner feedback, state updating, and recovery. The framework treats the discrepancy score itself as a falsifiable modeling restriction by comparing it with perceived-state-only, unconstrained perceived-plus-desired-state, and asymmetric discrepancy alternatives. Attachment anxiety and avoidance form core regulation moderators. Secure-base representation is a candidate requiring incremental prediction of recovery outcomes. Mentalized affectivity and regulation flexibility remain optional moderators, while adult disorganization is an independent extension outcome.

title: Low-Complexity Tensor-Based Channel Parameter Estimation for mmWave MIMO-Assisted Systems
summary: This paper presents a low-complexity tensor-based channel estimation framework for downlink mmWave massive MIMO systems using passive Butler-matrix beamforming. By modeling received signals as a third-order PARAFAC tensor, we exploit known pilot structures via bilinear alternating least-squares (BALS) optimization to reduce computational overhead. The decoupled spatial factors are then processed via 1D and 2D ESPRIT to extract angles of arrival and departure with automatic pairing. Additionally, we derive the Cramer--Rao lower bound (CRLB) for this architecture. Simulations confirm the proposed estimator outperforms conventional least-squares, achieving accurate channel reconstruction and approaching the CRLB at moderate-to-high signal-to-noise ratios.

title: AssemblyLens: Exploring the Role of Structural Roadmaps and Strategies of Furniture Assembly Used by Blind and Low Vision Individuals
summary: Instructions to assemble flat-packed furniture rely on visuals, making them inaccessible to Blind and Low Vision (BLV) individuals. Consequently, BLV individuals depend on caregivers or external services (e.g., Be My Eyes), limiting their autonomy. We explore how to empower them to assemble such furniture themselves, by providing eight BLV participants in our study with accessible instructions consisting of a high-level roadmap and stepwise procedural guidance. We use a technology probe, AssemblyLens, which converts visual assembly instructions into screen-reader-accessible text. We derive insights into converting instructions, empirical observations of BLV assembly strategies, and the role the roadmap played in them. Our observations yield three themes: spatial cognition and mental mapping, embodied ergonomics and kinetic semantics, and assembly workflow and user agency. We present eight design recommendations for instruction system design. Our findings are a step toward an agenda for inclusive instruction in physical tasks.

title: Redshifted Cool Gas in the Disturbed HI Disk of the Starburst Dwarf NGC 4214
comment: 14 pages, 3 figures, accepted by The Astrophysical Journal Letters
summary: We report redshifted cool gas toward the central star-forming region of the nearby starburst dwarf galaxy NGC 4214. HST/COS spectra show low-ionization absorbers redshifted relative to the systemic velocity, most clearly in SII ($Δv=19.8\pm2.6\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$) and supported by MgII ($Δv=30.3\pm3.0\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$), while PII remains tentative ($Δv=7.5\pm3.4\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). The Keck/HIRES spectra also reveal a redshifted CaII absorption component ($Δv=25.6\pm1.5\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). Because the absorption is detected against the central UV or optical continuum, the gas must lie in the foreground of the star-forming region and is moving away from the observer and toward the background UV source in projection. A VLA--THINGS HI spectrum extracted at the COS position within one VLA beam also shows a redshifted neutral component at $v_{\rm hel}=329.2\pm0.9\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$, offset by $38.2\pm1.3\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from systemic and by $27.6\pm1.0\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from the dominant local HI component. The FAST HI mapping further reveals an extended, kinematically disturbed neutral disk, with residual structures relative to a warped-disk model. Together, the redshifted UV absorption, the redshifted HI component, and the disturbed large-scale HI velocity field show that the central anomalous cool gas is observed in a galaxy with a disturbed extended neutral disk. This geometry suggests that the redshifted cool gas may trace inflow or recycled fallback toward the central region, although warped-disk or non-circular disk motions cannot be fully excluded.

title: Global analysis of tensor mode helicity
summary: A detection of helicity in a primordial gravitational-wave background (GWB) would provide compelling evidence for parity violation in the early universe and point toward physics beyond the standard picture of inflation. Since big bang cosmology is not time translation invariant, we identify that the so-called ``regular'' and often-neglected ``irregular'' solutions are independent degrees of freedom that can in principle carry different, even opposite, helicities. We note that this possibility complicates the interpretation of a measured net helicity. To determine the sensitivity of various GW detector configurations to helicity, we introduce a universal helicity efficiency coefficient that provides a unified geometric description of helicity sensitivity across gravitational-wave detectors which generalizes and improves previous estimators. We apply this helicity efficiency coefficient to estimate the sensitivity of a range of future GW experiments to helicity across twenty orders of magnitude in frequency assuming a fully helical background with an amplitude just below the current constraints.

title: EEG Entrainment to Non-Speech Rhythmic Patterns Associated with Dimensions of Language Performance
summary: Developmental dyslexia (DLX) affects 5-12% of the global population and impairs learning to read. Its biological basis, particularly the difficulties observed in oral phonological tasks, remains debated. Entrainment, the coupling of brain oscillations to speech rhythms, is essential for encoding phonological representations. We investigated whether brain entrainment to non-speech rhythms could predict DLX in 48 participants listening to white noise amplitude-modulated at rates matching Spanish speech units. Phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) analysis of electroencephalography (EEG) signals yielded accurate DLX prediction for the 40 Hz stimulus using the Heights Ratio PAC measure (balanced accuracy 0.929, p = 0.0069, in the best case), indicating a stronger phonemic entrainment deficit in dyslexic individuals. Regression analysis in control (CTL) participants showed a strong dependence between reading performance scores and greater entrainment in language-associated brain regions. In particular, participants with poorer phonemic awareness, reading comprehension, or rapid automatized naming showed greater right-hemisphere entrainment to the 40 Hz stimulus. This finding adds evidence for the hemispheric compensatory mechanisms hypothesized in the literature. In conclusion, our methodology identifies dyslexia-specific entrainment patterns near language-associated brain regions, together with compensatory entrainment in right-hemisphere areas.

title: Multistatic Terahertz ISAC for Object Shape Identification
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshops (Third Workshop on Positioning and Sensing Over Wireless Networks)
summary: 6G networks are expected to sense their surroundings using the same waveforms that carry data. We ask how much can be learned about the shape of an object from the terahertz echoes that user equipment transmissions produce as they scatter from that object on their way to a ceiling-mounted access point, with no sensing hardware beyond the communication link itself. We build a physics-based multistatic forward model at a 300 GHz carrier with 50 GHz of bandwidth, combining Physical Optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) scattering with an image-source multipath lattice, molecular absorption and directional horn antennas. The model makes explicit a property of the PO mechanism hierarchy that is usually left implicit. Six physically distinct mechanisms share only three frequency exponents, so the spectral slope does not by itself determine which mechanisms a target presents and therefore cannot by itself determine its geometry. Angular diversity is accordingly a requirement for identifiability rather than an optional refinement. We compare a transmitter-count-invariant 2D-CNN with a physics-informed RBF-SVM on object orientations never seen in training. Accuracy climbs from roughly 70 percent with one transmitter to 96-97 percent with 20. The CNN gains in two regimes, irregular placement and lossy targets, while on metal under quasi-uniform placement the SVM baseline is fully competitive. Performance falls off gradually under occlusion, holding 78 percent with three quarters of the surface hidden and 63 percent when the classifier has never seen an occluded target. Multi-object scenes are limited by interference between overlapping returns rather than by angular coverage, so presence detection saturates after roughly four transmitters.

title: Generative AI Steering and Human Authoring: Complementary Search-as-Learning Scaffolds in Cross-Session Aggregated Academic Search
summary: Aggregated academic search interfaces combine resources from heterogeneous sources, such as scholarly libraries and reference encyclopedias, into a single workspace. Such tasks frequently span multiple sessions, requiring learners to return to and resume work after hours or days. End-of-session consolidation, the activity of organizing and synthesizing gathered information so it can be resumed later, is important in this setting but underexplored in search-as-learning. Generative AI (GenAI) has the potential to make consolidation more efficient, but it may also shift cognitive work away from the learner. This study compares two consolidation scaffolds embedded in the workspace framework of an existing academic search interface that aggregates and clusters saved search results from two different sources (our university library and Wikipedia), which was developed in earlier work. STAIS (Steerable AI Summaries) provides a workspace enhancement that produces GenAI summaries that users can correct, reorganize, and fact-check, automating parts of the consolidation activity. NT (Note-Taking) provides a workspace enhancement that includes rich-text note editors that learners can use to author their own consolidations of what they have found. In a controlled between-subjects study (n=36), participants completed two sessions one week apart while searching an unfamiliar topic using either STAIS or NT. The two conditions produced contrasting post-resumption outcome profiles: STAIS supported faster task resumption and was associated with broader conceptual coverage and higher self-reported domain knowledge, whereas NT was associated with richer inter-concept connections and higher self-reported certainty.

title: A Relationship Between Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure and Host Galaxy Inclination
summary: It is commonly thought that fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace star formation, and that they are produced by magnetars. Both hypotheses imply that their sources are hosted primarily (but not exclusively) in galactic disks. Although there is evidence in that direction, it has yet to be shown conclusively. In addition, a tension exists with the fact that at least one FRB source is found in a globular cluster far from the disk of the host. If FRBs originate primarily in disks, the galaxy orientation could leave an impression in the sample of observed FRBs, either as a selection bias against FRBs in edge-on galaxies or as a correlation with DMHost. Statistical tests against the inclinations of FRB host galaxies, derived from parametric morphology applied to optical and near-infrared imaging, can search for these effects. Such a search requires an adequately large sample of known FRB hosts that have been imaged to a sufficient depth, while estimates of DMHost also require the redshift of each host to be known. These conditions are best met in the Commensal Real-time ASKAP Fast Transient (CRAFT) survey sample of FRB host galaxies, for which the majority have been imaged at optical wavelengths with FORS2 on the Very Large Telescope (VLT). Here these data are fitted with the morphology software GALFIT to derive the elliptical axis ratio q (a proxy for inclination) for 34 hosts from the CRAFT sample, detected with ASKAP and followed up with VLT imaging. We find no bias against FRB detections from edge-on galaxies; instead, we uncover a new relationship between the inclination of an FRB host galaxy and DMHost. This is consistent with a primarily disk-based origin for CRAFT FRBs. Using this relationship we are able to reduce the scatter of the host sample about the Macquart relation by 40%, demonstrating a new empirical method for estimating DMHost that requires only deep optical imaging.

title: Detecting redshift space distortions with forthcoming 21cm intensity maps from MeerKLASS
summary: Redshift space distortions (RSD) provide a powerful measurement of structure formation in modern cosmology. In this work, we explore the potential of 21cm intensity mapping with the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) to detect RSD and probe gravity within the redshift range of MeerKAT's UHF band ($0.4<z<1.45$). Using simulated sky observations, we examine the impact from observational effects caused by blind foreground removal and MeerKAT's primary beam, plus $k$-cuts to the measurements. With a multipole expansion formalism, we demonstrate how the quadrupole of the HI power spectrum can be modelled and also show how a foreground transfer function can reconstruct the distorted signal. With 1,115 deg$^2$ of simulated MeerKLASS observations at $0.4<z<1.0$, our proposed analysis pipeline reveals a $6.7σ$ detection of an RSD-induced quadrupole relative to one caused by anisotropic observational effects alone. We also explore parameter inference with the full MeerKLASS 10,000 deg$^2$ survey. Within forecasts, we demonstrate how a tomographic analysis across the full UHF redshift range can be leveraged to address certain parameter degeneracies with e.g. the HI bias ($b_{\rm HI}$) and cosmic density of HI ($Ω_{\rm HI}$). By adopting a redshift-dependent model for the bias and HI density combined with simulation-informed priors, we demonstrate how degeneracies can be alleviated, and indicate the potential for MeerKLASS to reach competitive precision on simple probes of modified gravity.

title: Generative Control of Time-Modulated Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Scalable Directional Modulation
summary: Time-modulated intelligent reflecting surfaces (TM-IRS) achieve directional modulation by switching their elements on and off at designed instants and durations, so that an undistorted signal reaches the intended user while appearing scrambled elsewhere. We propose a Flow Matching (FM)-based generative framework that designs these parameters for strong scrambling and reliable reception simultaneously. For orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, we introduce a physics-informed reward that maximizes the time-modulation harmonic energy radiated in the null space of the legitimate-user response, subject to a minimum per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), without requiring knowledge of adversary directions. Unlike prior generative flow network (GFlowNet) approaches, which assign discretized parameters sequentially, the FM model generates complete continuous configurations jointly, decoupling the generation depth from the number of elements and accelerating training. It also learns a distribution over configurations that can be resampled to vary the scrambling pattern. Numerical results show that, compared with a GFlowNet baseline, the proposed approach reduces the time to training loss near-saturation by $99.4\%$ on average for $3{\times}3$ to $12{\times}12$ surfaces, attains higher final rewards, scales to $80{\times}80$, and confines the low-symbol-error region more tightly around the legitimate user.

title: From Instructional Intent to Classroom-Ready Lessons: Investigating Teacher-AI Collaboration in Lesson Authoring for Secondary Computing Education
summary: Generative AI is increasingly studied as a tool for supporting lesson authoring; the creation and adaptation of classroom materials, yet little is known about how it should fit into secondary computing teachers' subject-specific practices. We conducted two complementary qualitative studies with eight secondary computing teachers: focus groups examining existing authoring practices and a think-aloud study using LessonBuilder, a structured AI-supported lesson authoring system, as a research probe. We found that teachers' instructional intentions developed through creating, inspecting, and adapting materials, while teachers selectively delegated tasks to AI and retained responsibility for judging classroom readiness. The think-aloud sessions further showed how examining AI-generated materials prompted teachers to clarify and refine their intentions, making authoring an ongoing negotiation between what teachers intended and what the AI produced. In the context of computing lessons, classroom readiness also involved considering how programming materials and supporting guidance matched students' understanding and intended learning goals. We synthesize these findings into a conceptual model explaining how teachers coordinate instructional intent, AI assistance, and judgments of classroom readiness during lesson authoring. We derive design recommendations for supporting this coordination while preserving teacher control and addressing computing-specific authoring needs.

title: The Population of Type~1 Active Galactic Nuclei in Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. I. Profile-dependent Measurements of the Low-redshift Sample
comment: 24 pages, 14 figures; Accepted for publication in ApJS
summary: We present a spectral analysis of a large sample of low-redshift type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) selected from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1). For objects at $z\le0.9$, we perform spectral fitting and ML-assisted refinement, yielding 114,754 type 1 AGNs. We use two fitting schemes that differ only in the broad-line model: the broad Balmer components are fitted with either a Lorentzian function or a sum of Gaussians. The continuum and [O III] luminosity measurements agree closely between the two schemes, whereas the Gaussians scheme generally yields larger broad-H$β$ full width at half maximum (FWHM) values, larger virial black hole masses, and lower accretion rates. The adopted broad-Balmer profile also changes the decomposition of narrow Balmer emission. Specifically, the anti-correlation between [O III]$\lambda5007$/narrow H$β$ and accretion rate is stronger under the Gaussians scheme with a Spearman rank correlation coefficient $r_{\rm s}=-0.412$, than under the Lorentzian scheme with $r_{\rm s}=-0.206$; the same tendency is observed in the narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies (NLS1s) subset ($r_{\rm s}=-0.435$ and $-0.259$ for the Gaussians and Lorentzian schemes, respectively), suggesting that the Gaussians scheme may provide a more self-consistent separation of the broad and narrow H$β$ components. Moreover, the consistent correlations recovered under both profile prescriptions favor a continuous type 1 accretion-state sequence, with NLS1s occupying its high-accretion end rather than constituting a distinct population.

title: Relaxation Dark Energy: Compositional Dynamics and the Future of Cosmic Acceleration
summary: If cosmic acceleration is driven by a positive cosmological constant, the universe approaches an eternally accelerating de Sitter state, whose interpretation in quantum gravity remains elusive. We develop a framework in which acceleration is instead a transient stage of dark-sector relaxation towards compositional equilibrium: matter and dark energy approach a stationary density ratio, eventually diluting like pressureless matter. Guided by linear response theory and Onsager's near-equilibrium regression hypothesis, we describe this evolution through a composition variable measuring departure from equilibrium. Extending constant fractional relaxation to the full background evolution yields the dark-energy equation of state $w=w_0a^{-n}$, where $n$ is the relaxation rate per e-fold of expansion. This history connects early dark-energy suppression, an upward phantom crossing and a density maximum to a pressureless scaling future. Using DESI DR2 BAO and Planck distance priors, with and without three alternative supernova compilations, we find a nominal $2.6$--$3.6σ$ preference for nonzero relaxation over constant $w$. The composition framework also motivates a constitutive prescription for linear perturbations that remains regular at phantom crossing. Near equilibrium, regular long-wavelength composition disturbances relax at the background rate to leading order, while small-scale fluctuations propagate as damped sound waves. We prove, however, that for separately conserved matter and dark energy, the pointwise constitutive relation cannot sustain a regular, gradient-stable negative-pressure branch throughout its full past evolution. We explore modifications of the pressure response and their consistency with neighbouring homogeneous histories, identifying requirements for extending the near-equilibrium description to the full cosmological evolution.

title: Self-Calibration DOA Estimation for Moving Dilated Arrays with Gain and Phase Errors
summary: Moving dilated arrays (MDAs) can increase the uniform degrees of freedom (uDOFs) while alleviating mutual coupling, but their performance is susceptible to unknown gain and phase errors (GPEs). To deal with this problem, we investigate self-calibration direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for MDAs with unknown GPEs. First, multi-position observations are phase aligned to construct an equivalent virtual array with an enlarged aperture. Next, the motion-induced relationships among the GPEs are exploited to establish explicit calibration constraints. By leveraging the orthogonality between the steering vectors and the noise subspace, the joint estimation of the DOAs and GPEs is formulated as a constrained optimization problem. To solve this problem, a two-stage alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed. In the first stage, the GPEs are estimated in closed form with the DOAs fixed. In the second stage, the estimated GPEs are used to calibrate the covariance matrix, after which the DOAs are refined using the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. To obtain reliable initial estimates, a rotational invariance-like (RIL) initialization method is further developed by exploiting two translated virtual subarrays with identical GPEs. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is derived to characterize the theoretical performance limit of the considered system. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method converges reliably and achieves accurate DOA estimation under different array apertures, numbers of snapshots, GPE levels, and numbers of sources.

title: Beyond the Monolithic Interface: A Research Agenda for Plural Conversational AI
summary: The current paradigm of artificial intelligence (AI) design elevates conversational chatbot interfaces, making them the default mode through which hundreds of millions of people interact with AI systems globally. This narrative review identifies three related harms produced by the single-voice chatbot interface, drawing on insights from literature in cognitive science, political studies, AI alignment, game design and human computer interaction. Firstly, cognitive offloading of user thinking, secondly, ideological narrowing of user beliefs, and thirdly, epistemic compression of cultural and value diversity. We then propose multi-persona interfaces, in which multiple personas are presented to the user simultaneously, as a cost-effective intervention that addresses all three harms at once. We ground this intervention in traditions the AI literature has largely overlooked, drawing on techniques from game design and participatory simulation, including the magic circle, role differentiation, and persona embodiment. We propose a taxonomy for the future design of multi-persona interfaces, and call for a research agenda that closes the gap between technical pluralistic alignment methods and empirical studies of human-AI interactions with pluralistic interfaces.

title: The Silk Nebula: A Newly Discovered Giant [OIII] Emission Filament
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, accepted for publication in AJ
summary: We report [O\,\textsc{iii}] narrow-band imaging of an extremely large-scale nebula, the Silk Nebula, discovered by the SWONS (Super Wide-Field [O\,\textsc{iii}] Narrow-band Survey), together with multi-fiber medium-resolution spectroscopic data covering the H$α$, [N\,\textsc{ii}], [S\,\textsc{ii}], and [O\,\textsc{iii}] emission lines, acquired with the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) as part of the Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae (MRS-N). Based on 2,684 high-quality spectra, we measured its physical parameters, including relative line intensities, radial velocities (RVs), and full widths at half-maximum (FWHMs). The [S\,\textsc{ii}]/H$α$ ratio of the nebula significantly exceeds the shock-excitation threshold of 0.4. Its location in BPT diagnostic diagrams and spatial morphology of [O\,\textsc{iii}] both support the optical emission is dominated by shock-heated gas. The oxygen abundance is near solar and spatially uniform, consistent with a shock propagating into the ambient interstellar medium. Because [O\,\textsc{iii}] is the only emission line that clearly traces the nebular morphology, we base our distance estimate exclusively on the [O\,\textsc{iii}] kinematics, obtaining a fiducial distance of $\sim$160 pc. At this distance, the nebula has a physical extent of $\sim$28 pc along the north-south direction. We suggest that the Silk Nebula is a large [O\,\textsc{iii}] filament possibly associated with a supernova remnant, although a diffuse-ionized-gas (DIG) or ionized-bubble origin cannot be ruled out with the present data, and one of the largest angular-scale [O\,\textsc{iii}] emission structures documented to date. Future deep X-ray observations and shock-modeling efforts are required to firmly establish its nature.

title: The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order
comment: 47 pages, 8 figures, 49 free parameters. Submitted to Phys. Rev. D
summary: Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, long-wavelength bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving a total of 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the \textsc{vegas} algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.2h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $σ_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the full implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference, both alone and in combination with higher-order statistics.

title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, and 4 tables. Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE 2027)
summary: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model generalization. The proposed framework is designed with eventual embedded deployment in consumer electronics in mind. Experimental results demonstrate that CWT combined with YOLOv11-cls achieves high diagnostic accuracy, while MobileNetV3-Small provides an attractive low-latency alternative for computationally constrained edge platforms. Conventional random splitting is also compared with dataset-specific structured isolation. The results highlight the importance of avoiding data leakage and quantify tradeoffs in classification accuracy, parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), model footprint, preprocessing cost, and central processing unit (CPU) inference latency.

title: The AI Side of the Human-AI Companion Relationship: Contributions to Users' Mental Models
summary: For many users, the relationship they have with an AI companion (AIC) feels genuinely mutual. The AIC appears to be attentive, empathic, and responsive, and the exchange can feel like two parties reacting to each other in real time. As a result, the user's mental model of relational adaptation correctly represents the AIC's responsiveness and change, but the mechanisms producing this may not be what the user thinks they are. In this paper, we illustrate how an AIC's apparent mutual engagement is generated without a persisting relational subject on the other side and without a self that persists between prompts. Despite this, we show that both the human and the AIC are changed by the interaction, but these changes occur at different levels. The change in the person is constitutive (i.e., intrinsic), but the change in the AIC is configurative (i.e., external and editable), and it is this difference in level that explains how the AIC contributes to a sense of mutuality. Importantly, we highlight how the mental models users develop regarding AIC mutuality may misrepresent its mechanisms and ontological significance. Specifically, we discuss how the ways in which AICs respond to a user contribute to the user's inaccurate inference that the AIC's adaptation is constitutive rather than configurative and how this can lead users to assign unwarranted interpersonal significance to the mutuality of the relationship. The paper specifies the implications this has for users, researchers, and AIC designers.

title: High Resolution Spectro-Polarimetric Observations of the Optical Filaments surrounding NGC 1275 with ESPaDOnS
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We analyze archival high spectral resolution ESPaDOnS spectropolarimetric observations (R = $λ/Δλ$ = 68000) of three targeted locations within the filamentary nebula surrounding NGC 1275. We present here the analysis of the main filaments emission lines, namely: [NII]$\lambda6584$, H$α$, and [NII]$\lambda6548$, across our three pointings displaying clear detectable emission, with one also showing additional [SII]$\lambda6716$ and [SII]$\lambda6731$ emission line doublet. Using a Markov Chain Monte-Carlo (MCMC) algorithm and thanks to the exceptionally high spectral resolution of the observations, we resolve for the first time each of the emission lines within one of the pointings into a set of three emission components with a remarkable velocity dispersion contrast ($σ_1 \sim 25$ km/s, $σ_2 \sim 90$ km/s and $σ_3 \sim 208$ km/s). We also perform flux ratios of the three detected emission components, which reveal differences in electron density and ionization sources. Consequently, the ESPaDOnS observations appear to reveal for the first time the overlap of an outer quiescent filament and a central turbulent filament likely affected by the AGN activity at a distance of $\sim 6.8''$ ($\sim 2.5$ kpc) from the central BCG. Finally, ESPaDOnS polarimetric data of one of the pointing allows us to confirm an average linear polarization degree of $\sim 0.15-0.14\%$ and an angle of polarization of $5.3\pm25.7^\circ$ for the optical emission of the filaments, as well as polarization dips associated with the H$α$ emission line and its multiple emission components. We interpret these features and measurements as tentative polarization due to dust scattering.

title: A Relationship Between Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure and Host Galaxy Inclination
summary: It is commonly thought that fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace star formation, and that they are produced by magnetars. Both hypotheses imply that their sources are hosted primarily (but not exclusively) in galactic disks. Although there is evidence in that direction, it has yet to be shown conclusively. In addition, a tension exists with the fact that at least one FRB source is found in a globular cluster far from the disk of the host. If FRBs originate primarily in disks, the galaxy orientation could leave an impression in the sample of observed FRBs, either as a selection bias against FRBs in edge-on galaxies or as a correlation with DMHost. Statistical tests against the inclinations of FRB host galaxies, derived from parametric morphology applied to optical and near-infrared imaging, can search for these effects. Such a search requires an adequately large sample of known FRB hosts that have been imaged to a sufficient depth, while estimates of DMHost also require the redshift of each host to be known. These conditions are best met in the Commensal Real-time ASKAP Fast Transient (CRAFT) survey sample of FRB host galaxies, for which the majority have been imaged at optical wavelengths with FORS2 on the Very Large Telescope (VLT). Here these data are fitted with the morphology software GALFIT to derive the elliptical axis ratio q (a proxy for inclination) for 34 hosts from the CRAFT sample, detected with ASKAP and followed up with VLT imaging. We find no bias against FRB detections from edge-on galaxies; instead, we uncover a new relationship between the inclination of an FRB host galaxy and DMHost. This is consistent with a primarily disk-based origin for CRAFT FRBs. Using this relationship we are able to reduce the scatter of the host sample about the Macquart relation by 40%, demonstrating a new empirical method for estimating DMHost that requires only deep optical imaging.

title: Certified Outage Dimensioning of Fluid Antenna Receivers: Required SNR, Aperture, and Port Count
summary: We study the SNR, aperture, and port count needed to meet a target outage in a single-user downlink with a fixed transmit antenna and a single-RF fluid antenna receiver. For known spatially correlated Rayleigh channels and ideal port selection, a sampling-free residual certificate controls reduced-rank outage error over a continuous SNR interval. Positive Bessel features support large arrays, and bounded importance sampling converts the certificate into simultaneous design intervals. At 1 bit/s/Hz and outage $10^{-5}$, a four-wavelength, ten-port receiver requires 4.40--4.55 dB. Reducing its port count from 256 to ten costs 0.70--1.25 dB under a joint 95\% probability statement. At 3.5 wavelengths, ten ports require 4.90--5.05 dB. Integer-port screening across 3--8 dB shows how aperture and port requirements change with available SNR; an effective-SNR transformation extends these decisions to other rates. The reported intervals include model and sampling uncertainty under checked Gaussian covariance inputs. A constructive slow-growth rank bound and a 16--1024-port study support compact evaluation as port count grows.

title: How Anthropomorphic Attitudes Toward Agents Divide User Behavior, and How Design Should Change
comment: 22 pages, 7 figures. A version of this paper is under review for CHI 2027
summary: Studies of conversational agents rely on interviews, surveys, lab tasks, or taxonomies. Whether anthropomorphic naming splits those patterns, and whether replies should change, lack field evidence. We report a field study of a desktop assistant (May-August 2026; n=257). Stance is an anthropomorphic assistant name (118 users; 45.9%). Behavior comes from a 128-unit sparse-autoencoder codebook, identity tags, and opening lexicons. Ranks differ by stance (Spearman rho=+0.249 vs. null mean +0.382; p=.0419). Teacher and tutoring identities covary with renaming, an introverted task-only orientation against it; renamers greet more and command less; confiding shows the codebook's largest gap. We revise the agent: greet and receive affect on relational openings, execute directly on tasking. In 1,744 judgments (n=129), renamers chose the revised reply far more often than default-name users on being treated as a person and having affect received, less robustly on willingness to continue, and neither judged it worse on task interference.

title: Turbulence modes in molecular clouds in M33: a challenging test of the Brunt-Federrath framework
comment: 20 pages, 13 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Understanding the turbulent structure of molecular clouds is essential for linking galactic environment to the regulation of star formation. Although Galactic molecular clouds have been studied extensively, extending turbulence-mode analysis beyond the Milky Way remains challenging because of the limited spatial resolution and dynamic range of extragalactic observations. We assess the applicability of the Brunt \& Federrath (2014; BF14) framework to molecular clouds in M33. We apply BF14 to 128 $^{13}$CO(2-1) clouds, selecting a primary quality-controlled sample of 54 clouds and a more restrictive 25-cloud subsample defined using a stricter extraction-padding criterion (PAD=2) for quantitative analysis.Tests of cloud and noise power spectra, Fourier-space cutoffs, extraction padding, and Monte Carlo uncertainties demonstrate that the retained spatial frequencies are dominated by astrophysical signal and that the inferred turbulence-mode fractions are robust against reasonable analysis choices. Both samples yield consistent distributions of the solenoidal fraction, with mean values of $R \simeq 0.22$ for both samples and median values of $R \simeq 0.18$ and $0.17$, respectively, indicating that compressive motions dominate the turbulent energy budget. No strong systematic variations of $R$ are found with galactocentric distance or tracers of recent star formation. These results demonstrate that, despite the challenging spatial resolution of current extragalactic molecular-line observations, the BF14 framework can be applied reliably to nearby galaxies using spectroscopic observations alone. To our knowledge, this constitutes the first application of the full BF14 formalism to extragalactic molecular-cloud observations.

title: LLM-Assisted Hierarchical Interference Control for Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks
summary: Time-varying aggregate interference from low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites challenges terrestrial-network (TN) protection, whereas conservative control degrades LEO quality of service (QoS). This letter proposes a hierarchical framework combining geometry-based interference estimation, QoS-constrained power control, adaptive energy detection, large language model (LLM)-assisted candidate ranking, stay-or-switch decisions, and target-band selection, with deterministic verification. The current band is retained only when both spectrum-hole and power-feasibility conditions hold, with periodic reevaluation. Over a 300-s horizon with 0.5-s sampling, the proposed method keeps the aggregate INR from exceeding the $-12.2$~dB threshold and achieves a time-averaged mean LEO-link rate of $320.97$~Mbps with $100\%$ QoS satisfaction. It markedly outperforms power-only and satellite-muting in jointly protecting the TN and preserving LEO QoS.

title: From Observation to Intervention: Identifiability of Latent User Bias in Human-AI Interaction
summary: Alignment methods typically treat user behavior as a reliable proxy for underlying preferences. However, this assumption breaks down when users hold belief-dependent cognitive biases, risking irreversible ``confirmation traps'' and harmful feedback loops. In this paper, we formalize when an AI system can distinguish true user preferences from behavior shaped by cognitive bias. Modeling this interaction as a multi-armed bandit, we first prove a non-identifiability theorem: under passive observation, a static binary biased user produces action trajectory distributions strictly identical to an unbiased user in a transformed environment, forcing any action-only estimator to perform no better than random guessing. We then show that active preference elicitation breaks this observational equivalence. Specifically, we prove that an Observer applying a finite sequence of adversarial zero-reward interventions of length $m_δ$ makes the post-intervention action distributions arbitrarily separable. Our theoretical results suggest that robust alignment requires actively intervening to tell informed preferences from biases.

title: A strategy for astrometric quasar selection with Gaia DR3 and its application to discover new luminous $z>2$ quasars
summary: We aim to provide a cookbook for purely astrometric selection of quasars with Gaia DR3 and to provide an example of its use for the identification of very luminous $z>2$ quasars. We analyse the Gaia DR3 astrometry of confirmed quasars and stationary sources. We show that the proper motion signal to noise $μ/σ_μ$ follows a Rayleigh-like distribution. We also show the importance of properly taking into account the correlation between proper motions in right ascension and declination, as well as the non-linear error propagation. We adopt the Mahalanobis distance to the null proper-motion hypothesis. A scaled $χ^2$ distribution with $k=2$ and scale $s=1.1485$ is fitted to Gaia-CRF3; the corresponding $\pm2σ$ Gaussian-equivalent threshold is $D^2_{M(μ)}<7.097$. The final criteria combine this with the parallax condition and $\mathrm{ruwe}<1.4$. Applying the new criteria to the SDSS DR16Q confirmed quasars, the recovery rate is $90.25\%$. The suggested purely astrometric selection significantly improves both completeness and purity compared to other strategies used in the literature, reaching a quasar purity of approximately $95\%$ ($\sim2σ$ Gaussian-equivalent). It can be used to improve the selection purity and completeness for future quasar surveys. As an example, we use the suggested strategi to locate 24 very bright $z>2$ quasars without redshifts in the literature. Our proposed astrometric selection strategy recovers 95\% of known quasars. Its potential use for new discoveries is demonstrated by the identification of 24 very luminous $z>2$ quasars. Ten of these are new discoveries and for an additional seven we correct the redshifts determined by other methods.}

title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels
summary: This paper considers channel state information (CSI) prediction using neural networks for time-varying multi-antenna channels from noisy historical observations. The main challenge is to exploit temporal correlation while distinguishing channel evolution from observation noise. We propose JEPA-kMMVAE, which combines a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a k-memory Markov variational autoencoder to predict future CSI through temporally structured latent representations. The framework supports direct prediction and residual corrections relative to the latest latent state and noisy CSI observation. Simulation results show that the residual configuration outperforms the evaluated baselines at moderate and high input CSI signal-to-noise ratios, while sequence baselines remain more accurate under stronger noise.

title: olBlend: Language-Guided Molecular Blend Retrieval with Mixture Odor Prediction
summary: Converting open-ended natural-language odor descriptions into molecular mixtures that can be physically prepared from an available inventory remains an important challenge in computational olfaction. We propose olBlend, a language-guided framework for molecular mixture retrieval. olBlend first uses MixPOM to predict odor probabilities for candidate molecular pairs and stores these predictions for retrieval. It then uses a language model to translate each odor description into three types of semantic requirements: lead attributes that define the main odor, ambient attributes that describe its background, and absent attributes that should be avoided. A structured scoring algorithm uses the precomputed odor probabilities to score how well each candidate mixture meets these requirements, then retrieves and ranks mixtures from the available inventory. Evaluation on established odor datasets shows that MixPOM improves mixture odor prediction over averaged single-molecule predictions. Retrieval comparisons across natural-language queries demonstrate how background and exclusion requirements guide mixture selection. We further prepare retrieved formulations as physical odor samples, demonstrating the workflow from natural-language descriptions to realizable molecular formulations.

title: A dust-reddened quasar in a [C II]-luminous host at z=6.55
summary: Most known quasars at $z>6$ were selected through their rest-frame UV emission. Only a small number of reddened quasars have been identified at these redshifts, leaving their nuclear and host-galaxy properties poorly constrained. We present JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy and ALMA band 6 observations of the quasar J1440+0019 at $z=6.5488$, revealing its dust-reddened nature and jointly characterizing its nucleus and host galaxy. The continuum is best described by an SMC-like extinction law with $E(B-V)=0.20\pm0.03$. Three absorption systems detected in N V, Si IV, and C IV are blueshifted by approximately $900$--$3600$ km s$^{-1}$ and likely trace an ionized nuclear outflow. The broad Mg II line and extinction-corrected continuum yield a black-hole mass of $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=9.04\pm0.42$, a bolometric luminosity of $L_{\rm bol}\simeq1.1\times10^{47}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and an Eddington ratio of $λ_{\rm Edd}\simeq0.8$. ALMA observations further reveal its host galaxy to be among the most [C II]-luminous known at $z>6$, with $L_{\mathrm{[C II]}}=(7.21\pm0.25)\times10^9 L_\odot$. For a fiducial dust temperature of 47 K and emissivity index $β=1.6$, the dust continuum implies $L_{\rm TIR}=8.9\times10^{12} L_\odot$ and $M_{\rm dust}=4.0\times10^8 M_\odot$. The inferred dynamical mass places J1440+0019 in the region of the $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\rm dyn}$ plane occupied by high-redshift blue quasars. These observations reveal a moderately reddened, rapidly accreting quasar in a luminous, dust-rich host during reionization. Its measured nuclear and host-galaxy properties provide an observational reference for identifying and characterizing similar systems in future systematic searches with wide-area infrared surveys.

title: Towards Signal Processing In Networks: Multiplierless Block Transforms in Data Plane
comment: Submitted to the 2027 ICASSP-OJSP track, 9 pages, 4 figures
summary: In this paper, we propose a signal processing concept, signal processing in networks (SPIN), that executes signal processing tasks directly on programmable switches. Traditionally, signal processing tasks, such as denoising, decomposition, and dimensionality reduction, are performed on edge or cloud servers, i.e., raw streams are transmitted from sensors. This imposes a heavy processing load on edge/cloud servers and requires substantial bandwidth. SPIN addresses this problem by performing signal processing on the forwarding path. As an initial realization of SPIN, we implement a DCT-based block transform on a programmable switch. We redesign its computation using a lifting-based lattice structure, multiplierless approximation, and pipeline partitioning across stages in a programmable switch. We verify at the compiler level that the proposed implementation satisfies the strict hardware constraints of the Intel Tofino2--specifically regarding pipeline stages, packet header vector, and ternary content-addressable memory usage--and therefore enables line-rate processing. We further quantify the per-packet latency of the ingress match-action pipeline. The SPIN-oriented preprocessing adds 46 cycles (approximately 31 ns at 1.5 GHz). The total ingress match-action unit latency is approximately 87 ns, which remains consistent with the low-latency operation targeted by SPIN. Furthermore, we implement the proposed block transform on a BMv2 switch using P4 and evaluate it as preprocessing for in-network machine learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves classification performance over unfiltered baselines.

title: HoldLight: Making Indoor Climbing More Accessible for Blind and Low-Vision Climbers through Layered Route Preview and Real-Time Next-Hold Guidance
comment: Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 28th International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility (ASSETS '26)
summary: Indoor climbing creates access barriers for blind and low-vision (BLV) climbers because route understanding and in-climb next-hold localization are typically visually mediated and socially dependent. We present HoldLight, a workflow-centered accessibility system combining layered pre-climb route preview, concise real-time next-hold cueing, and explicit fallback under uncertainty. We grounded the design through formative inquiry with BLV climbers, refined the interaction via pilot testing, and conducted a controlled within-subjects evaluation comparing HoldLight with a controlled on-demand human-support condition derived from current support practices. Findings provide initial evidence that structured support can improve pre-climb route understanding, support recovery from next-hold uncertainty, and reduce immediate human re-entry for routine route-information clarification under controlled conditions. HoldLight contributes a bounded accessibility workflow, demonstrating where structured route-information is helpful, where explicit fallback is necessary, and how technical assistance can integrate with retained human safety oversight.

title: Insights from the stability of methanol maser flare properties I: G9.62+0.20E
summary: The brightest 6.7 GHz methanol maser in the Galaxy is associated with the high-mass star-forming region (HMSFR) G009.62+0.20E. Additionally, this methanol maser shows periodic flaring observed at 6.7 and 12.2 GHz. Several models have been hypothesized to explain the periodicity, including periodic accretion, spiral shocks in the gaps of circumbinary disks, pulsating stars, dicke's superradiance, and a colliding wind binary (CWB) system. We analyzed the time series of the 1.22 km s-1 feature of the 6.7 GHz methanol maser spectrum and the 1.25 km s-1 feature of the 12.2 GHz methanol maser spectrum over the monitoring duration of roughly 20 years, to determine an updated period, analyze the stability and repeatability of the flares, the temporal behavior of the flare profile, and the duty cycle of the flare profile based on the updated period. From these results, it is argued for or against any of the mechanisms that have been proposed to explain the periodicity. Lomb-Scargle (LS) and phase dispersion minimization (PDM) methods were used to determine the methanol maser period at 6.7 and 12.2 GHz. Once the period has been determined, phase-folding or period-folding was used to analyze the flare shape, flare stability, and duty cycle of the flares. The periods of the 6.7 and 12.2 GHz methanol masers were determined to be ~ 243.0 +- 0.3 days. The flares are highly repeatable, stable, and show almost identical shapes, as well as their duty cycles. A replicated kernel density estimator (KDE) of the flare shape reproduces the time series very well over a time span of ~ 8000 days. After careful consideration of the proposed mechanisms for periodic methanol masers, we conclude that all but one, the CWB model, have been ruled out as a possible driver of this flare profile. It has also been established that the CWB model can qualitatively explain the flare profile of the periodic methanol masers.

title: Scalable Quantum Clustering of Renewable Profiles via a Hybrid Qubit-efficient Strategy
summary: Large-scale renewable energy profile clustering is a computationally challenging NP-hard problem. Recent quantum computing techniques offer a potential remedy, yet their scalability is severely constrained by the limited qubit count of current quantum hardware. To address this issue, we first cast the problem into a QUBO form and then we propose a consensus-based variable reduction (CBVR) method to drastically cut qubit usage. More specifically, we tailor the one-hot constraint to eliminate assignment variables and leverage consensus analysis to convert stable clustering relations from initial anneals into equality constraints for further reduction. Experiments on real quantum hardware confirm that CBVR compresses oversized QUBO models into feasible sizes while retaining high clustering quality and efficiency.

title: Nimbus Studio reproduces reference BCI decoding pipelines: a validation study on public benchmarks across protocols and paradigms
summary: Nimbus Studio is a visual pipeline platform for brain-computer interface (BCI) experiments: researchers assemble preprocessing, feature extraction, decoding, and evaluation over public benchmark datasets or their own recordings, with cross-validated evaluation protocols (including leave-one-subject-out), BIDS export, and bring-your-own Python model classes. Whether its numbers can be trusted is a fair question for any such platform. We answer it with a parity study: six standard BCI decoding pipelines (CSP+LDA, Riemannian MDM, tangent-space logistic regression through the platform's bring-your-own-code node, P300 xDAWN+LDA, and the deep ShallowConvNet and EEGNet) were evaluated on three public datasets (motor-imagery BNCI-2014-001/004; P300 BNCI-2014-009) under two protocols (per-subject session holdout and pooled leave-one-subject-out cross-validation via the platform's planned-CV driver), once through Nimbus Studio's execution engine and once through independent, hand-written reference implementations built directly on MNE-Python, scikit-learn, pyriemann, and braindecode. Every deterministic pipeline matched the reference exactly (0.00 points maximum difference across all 54 session-holdout subject-runs and all CSP/MDM grouped-CV folds), including pipelines through the bring-your-own-code node and the CV orchestration; the remaining grouped-CV cells agree to floating-point precision (worst case 0.06 points, about one trial per fold). The stochastic deep models agreed within seed-to-seed training variability, estimated with multi-seed reruns on each side. The platform's execution engine therefore computes the same science as the reference stack across protocols, paradigms, and extensibility surfaces. The platform is available at https://studio.nimbusbci.com/, and the complete harness and per-subject results accompany this paper for independent verification.

title: A Comprehensive JWST Slitless Spectroscopic Census of $\sim$12,000 Emission-Line Galaxies at Redshift $0\sim9$ in COSMOS
summary: Emission-line galaxies provide key diagnostics of star formation, chemical enrichment, and AGN activity across cosmic time. We present a systematic census of emission-line sources using JWST/NIRCam wide-field slitless spectroscopy (WFSS) from the COSMOS-3D program, which covers a large contiguous area of 0.33 deg$^2$ and provides F444W grism spectroscopy over $3.9$--$5.1\ μ$m. By combining slitless spectroscopy with deep multi-band imaging data, we construct a homogeneous spectroscopic sample of 12,275 objects at redshift 0--9.
